top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) is a datable invention with an identifiable idea (magic-wavelength trapping that cancels the lattice light shift) and its decisive realisation at the 10^-18 level, reproduced with Sr, Yb and Hg in many laboratories and already delivering results (gravitational redshift at millimetre scale, constant drift bounds, dark-matter searches). It fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion with identifiable originators, the narrow citation keeps clear of the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and the two-name allocation is defensible though the credit tail (Lemonde, Takamoto, Yb and Hg groups) is a real cost. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a mature conceptual result but leaves the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal uncredited and lies close to the 2016 topology prize. P003 (twisted bilayer graphene) is a striking prediction plus discovery but is early, the origin of the correlated and superconducting states is unsettled, and Cao and others are left out. Any of the three is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I have no documented tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, and my TEM and materials background is adjacent to but not part of any slate proposal
